name: Node map
when: many parts, causes, or players, and the shape is unclear
prompt: {hint|Every arrow must be labelled with a verb: causes / blocks / needs / decides.}
readback: Reconstruct the graph; report hubs, orphans, and any edge labelled with a vague verb like relates to.

claims.claim: Building a concept map, made of nodes joined by labelled links, improves understanding and retention compared with reading, listing or outlining the same material.
Drawing a diagram of the causal relations in a problem improves causal reasoning about it compared with reasoning from text alone.
claims.construct: learner-generated diagrams and drawing; causal mapping

grounding.helps: when many parts, causes or players relate and the shape is unclear, and every arrow carries a specific verb such as causes, blocks or needs; building concept maps aids retention of studied material, but it is not a substitute for recalling it
grounding.backfires: when vague links like "relates to" stand in for real relations, when a finished map feels like understanding without being checked, when it grows too dense to read back from a photo, or when it replaces retrieval practice, which beat concept mapping as a study method
